stories.title: A Broken Pipe Slowed Down Firefighters in Clementi
stories.headline_kid: A special fire pipe inside a Clementi flat was broken, so firefighters had to drag heavy hoses up 8 flights of stairs during a fire.
summary: Last week, a fire broke out in a flat at Block 309, Clementi Avenue 4. Sadly, someone died in the fire. Firefighters from the Singapore Civil Defence Force (SCDF) rushed to help, but they ran into a big problem.

Tall HDB blocks have a special pipe system called a 'dry rising main'. It runs up the middle of the building like a straw, so firefighters can connect their hoses at any floor instead of carrying heavy equipment all the way up. But this pipe was faulty, so firefighters had to haul the heavy hose up eight floors by hand instead, which took precious extra time.
SCDF is now investigating what went wrong. The town council in charge of the building has been told to fix the pipe so it works properly next time.
This story reminds us how important it is for building safety equipment to always be checked and working, because in a fire, every second counts.

lenses.me: If you live in a HDB flat, this story shows why fire safety equipment in your building matters, even the parts you never notice.
lenses.family: Your family can ask if your block's fire safety equipment, like fire extinguishers and hose reels, is regularly checked.
lenses.friends: You and your classmates can talk about what to do if there's a fire at home — like knowing where the stairs are.
lenses.nation: Singapore takes fire safety in HDB blocks seriously, and town councils are responsible for keeping equipment like these pipes working.
lenses.world: Cities everywhere with tall buildings depend on these hidden safety systems, and this incident is a reminder for other places too.

stories.title: Opposition Party Wants a New Plan for Singapore's Future Economy
stories.headline_kid: The Workers' Party wants Parliament to talk about how Singapore should handle jobs, prices and new technology in the future.
summary: In Singapore's Parliament, different political parties can raise 'motions', which are like formal suggestions for the government to discuss and debate. The Workers' Party (WP), Singapore's biggest opposition party, is planning to raise a motion about building an 'economy of the future' for all Singaporeans.

WP Member of Parliament Kenneth Tiong said this is their way of answering big questions about jobs, cost of living, and how new technology like AI might change the way people work. He called it their own 'economic playbook', like a game plan for the future.
This motion will be debated in Parliament, where MPs from different parties will share their views. The government will respond too.
This matters because it affects things like what jobs might be available when today's Primary 5 pupils grow up, and how much things might cost in the future.

lenses.me: This debate is about the kind of Singapore you'll grow up and work in one day.
lenses.family: Your parents' jobs and how much things cost could be shaped by decisions like these.
lenses.friends: Your classmates will grow up needing new skills for jobs that may not exist yet, like ones related to AI.
lenses.nation: Singapore's Parliament regularly debates how to keep the country's economy strong and fair for everyone.
lenses.world: Many countries are grappling with how new technology will change jobs, and Singapore's debate is part of that bigger global conversation.

stories.title: 4 Singaporeans Caught in Vietnam Over Illegal Vape Drug Ring
stories.headline_kid: Police in Vietnam arrested 4 Singaporeans as part of a group accused of putting illegal drugs inside vape liquid.
summary: Police in Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam, arrested 65 people, including four Singaporeans and four Malaysians, for allegedly running an illegal drug network. The group is accused of injecting drug-laced e-liquid into vape pods, then selling these dangerous vapes to customers.

Vapes, or e-cigarettes, are already illegal in Singapore because they can harm your lungs and health. This case is even more serious because the vape liquid allegedly had narcotics, which are dangerous illegal drugs, mixed inside.
The arrests show how vape trafficking rings can cross borders, involving people from different countries working together. Vietnamese police are continuing their investigation into the network.
This is a reminder for young people never to try vapes, since you never truly know what might be hidden inside them.

lenses.me: This story is a strong reminder that vapes are illegal in Singapore and can be dangerous, sometimes hiding illegal drugs too.
lenses.family: Parents may want to talk to their children about the real dangers behind vaping trends among older students.
lenses.friends: If you ever see or hear about vapes being shared among friends, this shows why it's important to say no and tell a trusted adult.
lenses.nation: Singapore has strict laws against vapes and drugs to protect people's health and safety.
lenses.world: This case shows how criminal networks can operate across several countries in Southeast Asia, needing international police cooperation to stop them.

stories.title: Ferry Catches Fire Near Indonesia, Many Still Missing
stories.headline_kid: A passenger ferry caught fire at sea near Indonesia — five people died, and dozens are still missing.
summary: A ferry called Mutiara Sentosa 2 caught fire while sailing in the waters off Madura Island in Indonesia. There were many passengers on board, and rescue teams worked quickly to save people.
Sadly, five people have died, and 41 others are still missing after the fire. The good news is that 225 people have been rescued so far by search and rescue teams.

Ferries are a common way for people to travel between islands in Indonesia, much like how some Singaporeans take ferries to nearby islands like Batam or Bintan. This incident is a sad reminder of how important safety checks are on ships, especially fire safety equipment.
Rescue efforts are still ongoing, and Indonesian authorities are investigating what caused the fire.

lenses.me: If your family ever travels by ferry, this story shows why it's important that ships always follow safety rules.
lenses.family: Families planning ferry trips to nearby islands can ask about safety measures like life jackets and fire exits before boarding.
lenses.friends: You can share with friends why it's important to listen carefully to safety briefings whenever travelling by boat or ship.
lenses.nation: Singapore has strict maritime safety rules, partly because incidents like this remind countries how important it is to keep improving ship safety.
lenses.world: This tragedy highlights the dangers people in the region face when travelling by sea, and the importance of strong rescue systems.

stories.title: Why Are Big Department Stores Disappearing From Malls?
stories.headline_kid: Metro, a well-known department store, is closing its last two shops — and it makes us wonder if huge stores in malls are becoming a thing of the past.
summary: Metro, a department store you might recognise at Paragon or Causeway Point, announced it will close its last two stores. Department stores like Metro sell many kinds of things under one roof, from clothes to home items, similar to a mini-mall inside a mall.

These big stores are called 'anchor tenants' because, like a ship's anchor keeps it steady, they help keep a whole mall stable by drawing in lots of shoppers. When people visit the anchor store, they often end up shopping at smaller stores nearby too.

But more people are shopping online these days, using apps and websites instead of walking through big stores. This has made it harder for large department stores to attract enough customers to stay open.
Malls in Singapore may need to find new ways to attract shoppers, perhaps with more restaurants, entertainment, or smaller specialty shops instead of one giant department store.

lenses.me: The malls you visit with your family might look a little different in future, with fewer giant stores and more smaller shops or activities.
lenses.family: Your family's favourite department store might change or close, so it's interesting to see how shopping habits are shifting.
lenses.friends: You and your friends might notice more online shopping happening at home instead of big family trips to department stores.
lenses.nation: This shows how Singapore's retail and mall business is changing as more people shop online.
lenses.world: Many countries are seeing the same trend, where online shopping is changing how traditional stores and malls operate.
